name: Scapular Pull-Up
movementPattern: Scapular depression and retraction - hanging straight-arm pull
grip: Overhand pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder-width, thumbs wrapped securely.
description: Hang from a pull-up bar with completely straight arms and initiate vertical movement exclusively through scapular depression and retraction, elevating the torso without bending the elbows.
setup: Grasp an overhead pull-up bar with an overhand pronated grip slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Hang freely with arms completely straight in a relaxed dead hang, feet together and core braced.
Ensure elbows remain locked and motionless throughout.
instructions: Depress and retract your shoulder blades by pulling them down and together toward your spine.
Feel your chest lift and your body rise slightly (2 to 4 inches) toward the bar solely from scapular movement.
Hold the peak scapular retraction and depression for 1 to 2 seconds.
Slowly relax your shoulder blades back up toward your ears into the full dead hang under control.
cues: Pull shoulder blades down into your back pockets.
Keep arms completely straight without bending elbows.
Pause and squeeze at the top of the shrug.
commonMistakes: Bending elbows to pull with the arms rather than isolating the scapulae.
Swinging the legs or kipping to create momentum.
Rushing through the movement without holding peak depression.

logging.note: Strict straight-arm movement; count repetitions with full scapular range of motion from passive dead hang to active depression.

variantNote: Straight-arm scapular isolation movement training lower trapezius and latissimus engagement at the initiation of vertical pulling movements.
reviewNotes: Elbows must remain completely straight in both panels; panel A shows passive dead hang with elevated shoulders, panel B shows depressed scapulae with chest lifted.

sources.title: ExRx.net - Pull-up
sources.scope: Scapular mechanics in vertical pulling, lower trapezius activation, and hanging shoulder depression.
